2607.11250.title: Multi-Agent LLMs Fail to Explore Each Other
2607.11250.paper_summary: Exploration is essential for reliable autonomy in multi-agent systems, yet it remains unclear whether large language model (LLM) agents can explore effectively when interacting with one another. We show that modern LLM agents fail to do so, often exhibiting myopic and polarized interaction patterns that lead to suboptimal coordination and increased regret. We formalize this challenge as the Multi-Agent Exploration problem, modeling it as a partially observable stochastic game (POSG) problem in which agents must probe peers to infer their capabilities and identify effective interaction strategies. To address this, we introduce Multi- Agent Contextual Exploration (MACE), a lightweight framework that explicitly promotes exploration through structured peer selection. Across both contextual and parametric diversity settings, MACE substantially improves exploration behavior and downstream task performance. We further show theoretically that the value of exploration increases with agent diversity. Overall, our results highlight a fundamental limitation of current LLM agents and underscore the importance of explicitly guided exploration for reliable multi-agent autonomy. Code will be released in https://github.com/deeplearning-wisc/mace
2607.11250.paper_summary_zh: 探索對於多代理系統中的可靠自主性至關重要，但目前尚不清楚大型語言模型（LLM）代理在相互作用時是否能有效探索。<lb/>我們顯示現代LLM代理無法做到這一點，經常表現出短視和極端的互動模式，導致次優的協調和增加的悔恨。<lb/>我們將這一挑戰形式化為多代理探索問題，將其建模為一個部分可觀察隨機遊戲（POSG）問題，代理必須探查同伴以推斷其能力並識別有效的互動策略。<lb/>為了解決這個問題，我們引入了多代理上下文探索（MACE），這是一個輕量級框架，通過結構化的同伴選擇明確促進探索。<lb/>在上下文和參數多樣性設置中，MACE顯著改善了探索行為和下游任務表現。<lb/>我們進一步理論上表明，探索的價值隨著代理的多樣性而增加。<lb/>總體而言，我們的結果突顯了當前LLM代理的一個基本限制，並強調了明確引導探索對於可靠的多代理自主性的重要性。<lb/>代碼將在 https://github.com/deeplearning-wisc/mace 發布。
